Comment: Outer photoreceptors. Detect broadband luminance information and project to lamina. ROI external input source. noROI(input)
Output Semantics: Temporal luminance changes in local visual field represented as broadband light intensity signals

Comment: Inner photoreceptors. Detect color information (including UV sensitivity) and project directly to medulla. ROI external input source. noROI(input)
Output Semantics: Color information (UV/blue/green wavelength bands) represented as color-selective light intensity signals

Comment: Lamina monopolar cell L1. Main relay cell of ON pathway. Responds to brightness increases and projects to Mi1 Tm3 etc in medulla.
Output Semantics: Temporally filtered ON signal representing positive contrast changes (brightness increases)
Requirement: Transforms broadband light intensity signals from [U.R1-R6] into signals selectively responsive to positive contrast changes. Outputs temporally filtered ON signals to [U.Mi1] [U.Tm3] [U.Mi4] [U.Mi9] [U.Dm3] providing input to ON motion detection and orientation detection pathways.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives broadband luminance signals from [U.R1-R6] as input and sends signals to multiple medulla neurons ([U.Mi1] [U.Tm3] [U.Mi4] [U.Mi9] [U.Dm3]) and lamina [U.L2]. Consistent with requirement to receive photoreceptor signals and distribute ON signals to multiple downstream UCs.
Capability: Selectively extracts positive change components from input signal applies temporal filtering and transmits downstream. Combination of high-pass filtering and ON pathway selectivity. Neural implementation of classical ON/OFF pathway separation in visual neuroscience functionally homologous to vertebrate ON-type bipolar cells (Joesch et al. 2010 Nature). Temporal filtering properties contribute to optimization of responses to moving stimuli (Behnia et al. 2014 Nature).
Mechanism: Receives glutamatergic input from [U.R1-R6] and represents positive contrast as membrane potential changes. Specifically hyperpolarizes in response to photoreceptor depolarization (sign-inverting synapse) then generates adaptive responses through intrinsic membrane properties. Temporal filtering realized through synaptic transmission dynamics and membrane time constants. Transmits signals to downstream medulla neurons via cholinergic excitatory synapses.
Implementation: HPF([U.R1-R6]+) where HPF is high-pass filter and + indicates positive change (ON) component

Comment: Lamina monopolar cell L2. Main relay cell of OFF pathway. Responds to brightness decreases and projects to Tm1 Tm2 etc in medulla.
Output Semantics: Temporally filtered OFF signal representing negative contrast changes (brightness decreases)
Requirement: Transforms broadband light intensity signals from [U.R1-R6] into signals selectively responsive to negative contrast changes. Outputs temporally filtered OFF signals to [U.Tm1] [U.Tm2] [U.Tm4] providing input to OFF motion detection pathway.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives broadband luminance signals from [U.R1-R6] as input and sends signals to multiple medulla neurons ([U.Tm1] [U.Tm2] [U.Tm4]) and [U.L1]. Bidirectional connection with [U.L1] represents electrical coupling (gap junctions) enabling ON/OFF pathway interaction. Consistent with requirement.
Capability: Selectively extracts negative change components from input signal applies temporal filtering and transmits downstream. Combination of high-pass filtering and OFF pathway selectivity. Electrical coupling with [U.L1] enables contrast information exchange between ON/OFF pathways contributing to visual adaptation and contrast normalization (Joesch et al. 2010 Nature).
Mechanism: Receives glutamatergic input from [U.R1-R6] hyperpolarizes in response to photoreceptor depolarization similar to [U.L1] but subsequent processing generates responses selective for negative contrast. Electrically coupled to [U.L1] via gap junctions current flow between pathways facilitates contrast adaptation.
Implementation: HPF([U.R1-R6]-) + α·[U.L1] where - indicates negative change (OFF) component and α is electrical coupling coefficient

Comment: Lamina monopolar cell L3. Additional relay cell receiving photoreceptor input within lamina cartridge.
Output Semantics: Luminance signal providing additional processing pathway (function partially unresolved)
Requirement: Provides additional processing pathway for photoreceptor input. Detailed function partially unresolved.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.R1-R6]. No defined outputs in current HCD. Consistent with being additional processing pathway.
Capability: R1-R6 input with different spatial-temporal filtering characteristics than L1 L2 presumed but details unknown.
Mechanism: Receives input from R1-R6 and performs specific processing but details unresolved.
Implementation: F3([U.R1-R6]) where F3 is specific temporal filter

Comment: Medulla intrinsic neuron Mi1. Receives input from L1 generates delayed response and outputs to T4 cells. Delay pathway for ON motion detection.
Output Semantics: Temporally delayed positive contrast signal
Requirement: Transforms temporally filtered ON signal from [U.L1] into temporally delayed signal. Outputs delayed positive contrast signal to [U.T4] implementing delay pathway in Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator model for ON motion detection.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L1] and outputs to [U.T4] as simple relay structure. Consistent with delay signal generation function described in requirement.
Capability: Adds temporal delay to input signal. This delay is essential element in Hassenstein-Reichardt motion detector generating direction selectivity by computing temporal correlation of signals from two spatially adjacent viewpoints (Takemura et al. 2017 eLife; Behnia et al. 2014 Nature). Delay timescale approximately 50-100 milliseconds optimized for motion speed range detected by flies.
Mechanism: Receives excitatory input from [U.L1] and generates temporal delay through synaptic transmission dynamics and intrinsic membrane properties. Specifically delayed response to input signal is generated through postsynaptic receptor desensitization and membrane time constants. Delayed signal transmitted to [U.T4] via glutamatergic excitatory synapses.
Implementation: [U.Mi1](t) = [U.L1](t - τ1) where τ1 is temporal delay (approximately 50-100 ms)

Comment: Medulla intrinsic neuron Mi4. Receives input from L1 and outputs to T4 cells. Additional input for ON motion detection.
Output Semantics: Additional temporal filter signal for positive contrast
Requirement: Provides additional input to T4 cells adjusting ON motion detection response properties.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L1] and outputs to [U.T4]. Parallel to [U.Mi1].
Capability: Provides different temporal filtering of L1 signal potentially adjusting temporal frequency characteristics and sensitivity of motion detection. Note: Detailed function not fully resolved in current research.
Mechanism: Receives input from L1 processes with different time constant and outputs to T4.
Implementation: F4([U.L1]) where F4 is specific temporal filter

Comment: Medulla intrinsic neuron Mi9. Receives input from L1 and outputs to T4 cells. Additional input for ON motion detection.
Output Semantics: Additional temporal filter signal for positive contrast
Requirement: Provides additional input to T4 cells adjusting ON motion detection response properties.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L1] and outputs to [U.T4]. Parallel to [U.Mi1].
Capability: Similar to Mi4 provides different temporal filtering potentially adjusting motion detection properties. Note: Detailed function not fully resolved in current research.
Mechanism: Receives input from L1 processes with different time constant and outputs to T4.
Implementation: F9([U.L1]) where F9 is specific temporal filter

Comment: Transmedullary neuron Tm1. Receives input from L2 generates delayed response and outputs to T5 cells. Delay pathway for OFF motion detection.
Output Semantics: Temporally delayed negative contrast signal
Requirement: Transforms temporally filtered OFF signal from [U.L2] into temporally delayed signal. Outputs delayed negative contrast signal to [U.T5] implementing delay pathway in Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator for OFF motion detection.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L2] and outputs to [U.T5]. OFF pathway version of [U.Mi1].
Capability: Similar to [U.Mi1] adds temporal delay to input signal. Provides delay pathway in OFF motion detection (Behnia et al. 2014 Nature).
Mechanism: Similar mechanism to [U.Mi1] generating delay through synaptic transmission and membrane properties.
Implementation: [U.Tm1](t) = [U.L2](t - τ2) where τ2 is temporal delay

Comment: Transmedullary neuron Tm2. Receives input from L2 generates non-delayed response and outputs to T5 cells. Non-delayed pathway for OFF motion detection.
Output Semantics: Temporally non-delayed negative contrast signal
Requirement: Transmits temporally filtered OFF signal from [U.L2] as non-delayed signal to [U.T5]. Implements non-delayed pathway in Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator for OFF motion detection.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L2] and outputs to [U.T5]. OFF pathway version of [U.Tm3].
Capability: Similar to [U.Tm3] transmits input signal with minimal delay.
Mechanism: Fast synaptic transmission immediately relays signal.

Comment: Transmedullary neuron Tm3. Receives input from L1 generates non-delayed response and outputs to T4 cells. Non-delayed pathway for ON motion detection.
Output Semantics: Temporally non-delayed positive contrast signal
Requirement: Transmits temporally filtered ON signal from [U.L1] as non-delayed signal to [U.T4]. Implements non-delayed pathway (immediate response pathway) in Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator for ON motion detection.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L1] and outputs to [U.T4]. Contrasts with [U.Mi1] forming non-delayed pathway.
Capability: Transmits input signal downstream with minimal delay. By pairing with delay pathway of [U.Mi1] two temporally offset signals are integrated in [U.T4] and multiplication-like nonlinear operation generates direction selectivity (Behnia et al. 2014 Nature).
Mechanism: Excitatory input from [U.L1] is immediately relayed to [U.T4] via fast synaptic transmission. Postsynaptic response time constant is short responding to input with almost no delay.

Comment: Transmedullary neuron Tm4. Receives input from L2 and outputs to T5 cells. Additional input for OFF motion detection.
Output Semantics: Additional temporal filter signal for negative contrast
Requirement: Provides additional input to T5 cells adjusting OFF motion detection response properties.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L2] and outputs to [U.T5].
Capability: Similar to Mi4/Mi9 adjusts temporal frequency characteristics of OFF motion detection.
Mechanism: Processes input from L2 and outputs to T5.
Implementation: F4([U.L2]) where F4 is specific temporal filter

Comment: Transmedullary neuron Tm9. Processes visual information in medulla and projects to LC cells in lobula. Relay of form vision pathway.
Output Semantics: Form vision feature signal integrating color information and spatial contrast patterns
Requirement: Integrates color information and spatial contrast providing input to form vision pathway. Processes color-selective signals from R7-R8 and distributes to multiple LC cells in lobula. Performs preprocessing for form vision feature extraction.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.R7-R8] and outputs to multiple LC cells ([U.LC4] [U.LC6] [U.LC10] [U.LC11]).
Capability: Processes color-selective signals from R7-R8 and distributes to multiple LC cells in lobula. Preprocessing stage for form vision feature extraction.
Mechanism: Receives glutamatergic input from R7-R8 performs spatial-temporal processing within medulla and projects to LC cells in lobula.
Implementation: Fcolor([U.R7-R8]) where Fcolor is color processing function

Comment: Transmedullary Y neurons. Receive input from Dm3 process orientation information and project to lobula. Show orientation-selective responses.
Output Semantics: Orientation-selective signal representing local contour orientation (edge direction)
Requirement: Realizes integration and transmission of orientation information. Receives orientation-sharpened edge signals from [U.Dm3] and enhances signals through mutual excitation among [U.TmY] cells with same orientation selectivity. Outputs orientation-selective signals representing local contour orientation to [U.LC6] used as form vision information for behavioral control.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.Dm3] has mutual excitatory connections among [U.TmY] cells and outputs to [U.LC6].
Capability: Enhances same-orientation information detecting contour continuity and facilitating contour integration. Enables extraction of clear contours even from noisy visual input (Ramos-Traslosheros et al. 2024 Nature).
Mechanism: Receives excitatory input from orientation-selective [U.Dm3]. [U.TmY] cells with same orientation selectivity have excitatory connections and cooperative activity enhances orientation signals.
Implementation: [U.TmY]θ = [U.Dm3]θ + μ·Σj [U.TmY]θj where θ is orientation μ is same-orientation excitation coupling coefficient and j represents spatially nearby [U.TmY] cells with same orientation selectivity

Comment: Distal medulla amacrine cell 3. Receives input from L1 shows orientation-selective responses. Performs mutual inhibition among Dm3 with different orientations and outputs to TmY.
Output Semantics: Edge signal of specific orientation sharpened by cross-orientation inhibition
Requirement: Realizes orientation detection. Extracts specific orientation (edge direction) from temporally filtered ON signal from [U.L1]. Further sharpens orientation selectivity through mutual inhibition among [U.Dm3] cells with different orientation selectivity. Outputs orientation-sharpened edge signals to [U.TmY] becoming input to contour integration pathway.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.L1] has mutual inhibitory connections among [U.Dm3] cells and outputs to [U.TmY]. Consistent with implementation of orientation-selective processing and cross-orientation inhibition.
Capability: Detects local contour orientation and enhances selectivity through cross-orientation inhibition. Similar to orientation selectivity mechanism in V1 simple cells forming basis for contour detection and form recognition (Ramos-Traslosheros et al. 2024 Nature).
Mechanism: Dendrites of [U.Dm3] are oriented along specific orientation responding selectively to edges along that orientation. [U.Dm3] cells selective for different orientations have inhibitory connections and competitive interaction sharpens orientation selectivity of each cell.
Implementation: [U.Dm3]θ = f([U.L1] ⊗ Gθ) - λ·Σφ≠θ [U.Dm3]φ where θ is orientation Gθ is Gabor-like spatial filter selective for orientation θ ⊗ is convolution λ is mutual inhibition strength and φ represents different orientations

Comment: T4 direction-selective cells. Receive input from Mi1 Tm3 etc and generate direction-selective responses to ON motion. Four subtypes respond to four cardinal directions and project to lobula plate.
Output Semantics: Direction-selective motion signal of positive contrast edges (four cardinal directions: front-back up-down)
Requirement: Realizes ON motion detection. Integrates temporally delayed positive contrast signal from [U.Mi1] and temporally non-delayed positive contrast signal from [U.Tm3] computing temporal correlation between spatially adjacent viewpoints to generate direction-selective responses. Additional inputs from [U.Mi4] [U.Mi9] adjust responses. Outputs direction-selective motion signals of positive contrast edges to [U.HS] and [U.VS].
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives multiple inputs (delay pathway [U.Mi1] and non-delay pathway [U.Tm3] adjustment inputs [U.Mi4] [U.Mi9]) and outputs to [U.HS] and [U.VS] performing wide-field motion integration. Consistent with direction-selective motion detection function described in requirement.
Capability: Nonlinearly integrates temporally offset signals from two spatially adjacent viewpoints generating direction selectivity. Neural implementation of Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator responding strongly only to motion in specific direction through multiplication-like nonlinear operation (AND-gate-like operation) (Takemura et al. 2013 Nature; Behnia et al. 2014 Nature). Four subtypes (T4a b c d) respond selectively to four cardinal directions (forward backward upward downward).
Mechanism: Receives input from [U.Mi1] (delayed) and [U.Tm3] (non-delayed) at different spatial positions on dendrites. Nonlinear integration within dendrites (e.g. voltage-dependent integration mediated by NMDA receptors) generates strong depolarization only when two inputs coincide spatiotemporally. This nonlinear integration generates responses selective for preferred direction motion. Four subtypes acquire different direction selectivity through spatial arrangement of dendrites and input combinations.
Implementation: Σi ([U.Mi1]i+Δ · [U.Tm3]i) + β·[U.Mi4] + γ·[U.Mi9] where i is spatial position Δ is offset in preferred direction · is nonlinear multiplication-like operation and β γ are adjustment coefficients

Comment: T5 direction-selective cells. Receive input from Tm1 Tm2 etc and generate direction-selective responses to OFF motion. Four subtypes respond to four cardinal directions and project to lobula plate.
Output Semantics: Direction-selective motion signal of negative contrast edges (four cardinal directions: front-back up-down)
Requirement: Realizes OFF motion detection. Integrates temporally delayed negative contrast signal from [U.Tm1] and temporally non-delayed negative contrast signal from [U.Tm2] computing temporal correlation between spatially adjacent viewpoints to generate direction-selective responses. Additional input from [U.Tm4] adjusts responses. Outputs direction-selective motion signals of negative contrast edges to [U.HS] and [U.VS].
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives OFF pathway delay pathway [U.Tm1] and non-delay pathway [U.Tm2] adjustment input [U.Tm4] and outputs to [U.HS] and [U.VS]. Forms parallel OFF motion detection pathway to [U.T4].
Capability: Similar to [U.T4] implements Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator but detects motion of negative contrast (dark edges). Parallel processing of ON/OFF motion detection enables visual system to simultaneously process motion of both bright and dark edges enhancing robustness of motion detection in complex natural scenes (Behnia et al. 2014 Nature).
Mechanism: Mechanism of [U.T5] is essentially same as [U.T4] but differs in that input comes from OFF pathway ([U.Tm1] [U.Tm2]). Direction selectivity generated through nonlinear integration in dendrites.
Implementation: Σi ([U.Tm1]i+Δ · [U.Tm2]i) + β·[U.Tm4] where i is spatial position Δ is offset and β is adjustment coefficient

Comment: Horizontal System cells. Wide-field tangential cells in lobula plate. Receive direction-selective input from T4/T5 and integrate horizontal wide-field motion. Output to descending neurons.
Output Semantics: Wide-field horizontal optic flow (self-motion and rotational motion components along front-back axis)
Requirement: Realizes wide-field horizontal motion detection. Spatially integrates direction-selective motion signals of positive contrast edges from [U.T4] and negative contrast edges from [U.T5] extracting horizontal optic flow patterns. Wide-field integration enhanced by interconnections among [U.HS] cells. Outputs wide-field horizontal optic flow to [U.DNOVS1] used for flight control.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives direction-selective input from many [U.T4] and [U.T5] performs wide-field integration through interconnections among [U.HS] cells and outputs to motor control system [U.DNOVS1].
Capability: By integrating outputs of many local motion detectors across wide field extracts optic flow patterns accompanying self-motion. Responds selectively to horizontal flow patterns accompanying translational motion in front-back direction and rotation around vertical axis (yaw). This wide-field integration suppresses local noise and motion of small objects enabling robust extraction of self-motion information (Suver et al. 2016 J Neurosci).
Mechanism: Receives excitatory input from many [U.T4] and [U.T5] across wide dendritic field. Responds strongly to consistent motion patterns across entire visual field through spatial summation. Furthermore [U.HS] cells are electrically coupled via gap junctions facilitating spatial smoothing and integration of motion information.
Implementation: Σxy (wh(x y) · ([U.T4]xy + [U.T5]xy)) + ε·Σj [U.HS]j where (x y) is position in visual field wh(x y) is weighting function for horizontal direction selectivity ε is electrical coupling coefficient and j represents adjacent [U.HS] cells

Comment: Vertical System cells. Wide-field tangential cells in lobula plate. Receive direction-selective input from T4/T5 and integrate vertical wide-field motion. Output to descending neurons.
Output Semantics: Wide-field vertical optic flow (self-motion components along up-down and roll axes)
Requirement: Realizes wide-field vertical motion detection. Spatially integrates direction-selective motion signals from [U.T4] and [U.T5] extracting vertical optic flow patterns. Wide-field integration enhanced by interconnections among [U.VS] cells. Outputs wide-field vertical optic flow to [U.DNOVS1] used for flight posture control.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface has same structure as [U.HS] performing integration selective for vertical direction motion.
Capability: Extracts optic flow patterns accompanying vertical translational motion and rotation around horizontal axes (pitch roll). Provides information essential for posture stabilization and altitude control during flight (Suver et al. 2016 J Neurosci).
Mechanism: Similar to [U.HS] but integrates input from [U.T4] and [U.T5] subtypes selective for vertical direction motion.
Implementation: Σxy (wv(x y) · ([U.T4]xy + [U.T5]xy)) + ε·Σj [U.VS]j where wv(x y) is weighting function for vertical direction selectivity

Comment: Lobula columnar neuron LC4. Detects small object motion in lobula and projects to central brain. Involved in behavioral control.
Output Semantics: Small object motion in local visual field (detection of small moving objects used for prey pursuit and conspecific tracking)
Requirement: Detects small object motion and transmits to central brain. Contributes to prey pursuit and conspecific tracking behavior.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.Tm9] and outputs to [U.OG-downstream].
Capability: Responds selectively to small moving objects. Suppresses background wide-field motion extracting local motion objects. Note: Detailed mechanism partially unresolved.
Mechanism: Realizes small object selectivity through input from Tm9 and local lateral inhibition within lobula.
Implementation: [U.LC4] = [U.Tm9] - ψ·Backgroundmotion where ψ is suppression coefficient

Comment: Lobula columnar neuron LC6. Detects looming stimuli in lobula and projects to optic glomeruli (central brain). Involved in avoidance behavior.
Output Semantics: Detection signal of expanding stimuli in visual field (looming detection representing approaching objects or collision danger)
Requirement: Detects looming stimuli (expanding objects in visual field) and transmits to central brain triggering avoidance behavior. Integrates form information from Tm9 and orientation information from TmY to detect approaching objects.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives inputs from [U.Tm9] and [U.TmY] and outputs to [U.OG-downstream].
Capability: Responds selectively to temporally expanding visual stimuli. Integrates form information from Tm9 and orientation information from TmY detecting approaching objects.
Mechanism: Integrates multiple inputs performing nonlinear operation detecting temporal expansion patterns.
Implementation: floom([U.Tm9] [U.TmY]) where floom is looming detection function

Comment: Lobula columnar neuron LC10. Detects visual features in lobula and projects to optic glomeruli.
Output Semantics: Specific visual feature patterns (function details partially unresolved)
Requirement: Detects specific visual feature patterns and transmits to central brain. Note: Detailed function not fully resolved in current research.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.Tm9] and outputs to [U.OG-downstream].
Capability: Processes form vision information from Tm9 presumed to respond selectively to specific visual features. Details unresolved.
Mechanism: Integrates input from Tm9 responding to specific patterns.
Implementation: f10([U.Tm9]) where f10 is feature detection function

Comment: Lobula columnar neuron LC11. Detects visual features in lobula and projects to optic glomeruli.
Output Semantics: Specific visual feature patterns (function details partially unresolved)
Requirement: Detects specific visual feature patterns and transmits to central brain. Note: Detailed function not fully resolved in current research.
Requirement realization by interface: Interface receives input from [U.Tm9] and outputs to [U.OG-downstream].
Capability: Similar to LC10 presumed to respond to specific visual features. Details unresolved.
Mechanism: Integrates input from Tm9 responding to specific patterns.
Implementation: f11([U.Tm9]) where f11 is feature detection function

Names: Descending neuron of ocellar and vertical system 1
Comment: Descending neuron of ocellar and vertical system 1. Receives electrical coupling and chemical synapses from HS/VS cells and transmits motion vision information to thoracic motor control system. ROI external output destination. noROI(output)
Optic glomeruli downstream neurons. Receive form vision information from LC cells and use for behavioral selection in central complex etc. ROI external output destination. noROI(output)
